Mapping thoughts after a quick look at the CSV:
- The Q3 projection (approx 22M tokens/month) is consistent with a small multi-school pilot.
- For nonprofits we commonly offer either: (A) one-time credits + pay-as-you-go, or (B) a small committed monthly credit with a discounted per-token rate for the duration of the pilot (3–6 months).

Tradeoffs:
- Option A (credit grant) is easiest operationally (no long-term commit) but unit cost after credits can be higher.
- Option B gives predictable unit economics and lower cost per token but requires a minimum monthly commitment and a short invoicing contract.

Given the fiscal sponsor / invoicing ask, Option B is the cleaner path operationally for finance. Typical minimums we’ve done for pilots like this: $2k–$5k/month (USD) depending on expected throughput. If they want zero minimum we can do Option A with a $X one-time credit (I’ll propose a number).

I’ll draft a MAP and proposed numbers tomorrow. Karthik, any compliance or procurement caveats we should anticipate when billing a sponsor instead of the nonprofit?

—Ben

Quick compliance notes:
- We need a signed billing authorization from the fiscal sponsor and a contact on their letterhead confirming the arrangement.
- SOC 2 / security questionnaire responses should be directed to procurement@redwood.com; if the sponsor requires encrypted invoices we can support that via our billing platform.
- If OpenCampus intends to process student PII, we’ll need to confirm data residency and any special audit logging; that’s separate from the credit approval but worth flagging.

I’ll prep a short checklist to include in the MAP so procurement has clear steps.

—Karthik
